transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-07-30
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Sara Liu (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Head of Data, MedBridge), Ravi Patel (CTO), Maya Ortiz (Product), Dr. Brian Kline (Clinical Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, rough): Goal is define quality eval plan + workload size + benchmarks to validate model selection and configuration for POC. Focus on golden prompts, regression test set, hallucination checks, scoring/thresholds, and infra cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time, I'm Evan from Redwood Inference, this call is to scope the poc and particularly the quality eval plan for the clinical summarization and extraction flows. Sara from our SE team is on to cover technicals.
[00:18] Sara: hey all, hi, quick agenda, we'll cover success criteria, workload sizing, how we'll run benchmarks, and the plan for golden prompts and regression tests, then timings. if anything's missing shout out.
[00:32] Laura: sounds good. our main ask - must not degrade clinical accuracy, and structured extraction like meds, dosages, and problem list needs to be near perfect. we have compliance windows so timeline is tight.
[00:46] Ravi: yeah timeline is important - execs want pilot results in 6 weeks. we can stretch to 8 weeks but prefer 4 weeks for initial signal. also we need to know if hosted or dedicated; data residency is a factor.
[01:05] Evan: understoood. typical POC we do is 4 weeks for initial bench + eval. we can do hosted with VPC peering or dedicated if you need reserved capacity. Sara, do you want to say a bit about the eval artifacts?
[01:18] Sara: sure. For quality eval plan we propose: golden prompts (a set of canonical prompts for each task), a regression test suite that includes edge cases, hallucination detection checks, format checks for structured output, and a scoring approach combining exact-match for structured fields and BLEU/rouge-like metrics + clinical-specific scoring for summaries.
[01:40] Maya: can you clarify golden prompts - is that just one prompt per task?
[01:46] Sara: yeah so golden prompts are a small curated set - maybe 50-200 examples per task depending on complexity. for structured extraction I'd aim 200 if you want statistical significance; for free-text summaries 100-200. these are the ground-truth prompts we use to evaluate model variants.
[02:02] Dr. Kline: and for hallucinations what do you measure? sometimes models invent diagnoses or meds - that is high risk for us.
[02:11] Sara: great question. we'll run hallucination checks two ways: 1) entity-level hallucination where model outputs entities not present in source (we flag any meds, allergies, procedures not in original), and 2) factual consistency checks for summaries - we run an automated fact-checker plus a human sample review. threshold proposal: entity hallucination rate <3% and summary factual-error rate <5% for passing the POC.
[02:40] Laura: those thresholds feel reasonable as starting points. do you have examples for the scoring rubric?
[02:46] Sara: yes. For structured fields we use exact-match/normalized-match (e.g., medication name normalization). Score = (correct matches) / (expected fields). For summaries, we score on 1) clinical correctness (human-labeled, 0-2 scale), 2) conciseness/format, 3) hallucination flags. aggregate pass threshold: weighted score >= 0.85. we'll share rubric in the template.
[03:09] Evan: quick note - we also track latency and cost per 1k tokens as secondary SLOs, since you'll need to balance throughput. Ravi, do you have throughput expectations?
[03:20] Ravi: at peak 30 concurrent requests, avg request size ~1.2k tokens, 95th latency target <800ms for summaries. cost - budget TBD but we want predictable unit economics.
[03:35] Sara: ok we'll size the workload. For 30 concurrent with 1.2k tokens, we'd recommend a dedicated pool for stable latency or hosted with reserved capacity. We'll produce a cost-latency table by model variant and quantization profile.
[03:50] Maya: about regression tests - how often will they run and what triggers?
[03:55] Sara: regression suite will run on each model variant we try during the POC - nightly runs for full suite if needed, quick smoke tests after config changes. the suite contains: golden prompts, adversarial edge cases, and a set of random sample traces from your supplied dataset. We'll also include format validators (JSON schema checks) so outputs are parseable.
[04:20] Laura: format is important - our downstream systems ingest a JSON with fields med_list, dosage, confidence. can you validate conf ranges and enforce required fields?
[04:30] Sara: yes - format checks include schema validation, field-level confidence thresholds (we can set minimum confidence for auto-ingest), and fallback flagging if schema fails.
[04:40] Evan: let's talk benchmarks. we typically run the following: baseline (your current model or rule-based), 2-3 open models (quantized variants), and Redwood-verified config(s). you'll get metrics: exact-match rates, hallucination rate, summary scoring, latency, and cost.
[05:00] Ravi: what's the time to run a full benchmark with 5k samples?
[05:05] Sara: rough estimate - with continuous batching and parallel workers, 5k samples for structured extraction is about 2-3 hours on dedicated infra; summaries take longer because they are generative, maybe 3-6 hours depending on sequence length. if we run on hosted with limited concurrency it could take a day.
[05:22] Laura: we'll start with 1k de-identified records to iterate quicker. is that enough to get signal?
[05:29] Sara: 1k is fine for preliminary signal, especially if you select stratified samples (common cases + edge cases). we'll ask for a sampling plan.
[05:36] Dr. Kline: do you support red-team style prompts to trigger hallucinations?
[05:40] Sara: yep we'll include adversarial prompts. examples: ambiguous contexts, truncated notes, contradicting prior history. We'll surface where model confidence is low and recommend fallback to human-in-loop.
[05:52] Maya: what's the scoring approach for the POC report? single composite score? multiple dashboards?
[05:58] Sara: both. final POC report will include a composite score per model for quick comparison plus breakout metrics per task. composite = weighted sum: structured extraction 50%, summary factuality 30%, hallucination penalty 15%, latency/cost 5% (weights adjustable). We'll include precision/recall, exact-match, and confusion matrices for entity types.
[06:25] Evan: acceptable pass criteria for pilot to be considered successful - suggestions?
[06:30] Sara: suggested pass criteria: structured extraction exact-match >= 92%, summary factuality score >= 0.88 (weighted), entity hallucination rate <3%, and 95th percentile latency <1s on dedicated pool. if you need stricter thresholds we can iterate.
[06:46] Ravi: those are aggressive but reasonable. we'll review internally and come back with must-have vs nice-to-have.
[06:52] Laura: what about privacy - can we run benchmarks in our VPC?
[06:56] Evan: yes we support a private deployment or hosted with VPC peering and controlled KMS. we'll share the infra checklist.
[07:04] Sara: also worth calling out caching: prefix/KV cache can dramatically reduce cost for repeated notes, but for one-off unique clinical notes caching helps less. We'll show cost delta in bench report.
[07:16] Maya: how will you surface regressions over time?
[07:20] Sara: we'll store test-suite results and produce regression alerts when a metric degrades by X% (configurable). For POC we snapshot a baseline run and compare subsequent runs to detect regressions.
[07:32] Dr. Kline: human review - how large should the human sample be for summaries?
[07:36] Sara: we recommend a stratified human sample of ~200 summaries for clinical review to estimate factual error rates with confidence. if you want lower margin of error, increase the sample.
[07:47] Evan: ok wrapping up - recap of owners and timeline: we'll send the quality-eval template + scoring rubric + golden prompt examples and ask MedBridge to upload 1k de-identified records. target to run first benchmark in week of 2026-08-10 with results by 2026-08-14. does that work?
[08:05] Laura: yes that timeline works for us if we can get the template this week.
[08:10] Ravi: I'll coordinate infra windows for the benchmark.
[08:14] Maya: we'll prepare sample selection and label guide.
[08:18] Evan: great, action items listed. we'll also attach SOC2 docs and SAML/SSO notes.
[08:24] Sara: shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/poc/quality-eval-template.xlsx, redwood/poc/golden-prompts (drive link), infra-checklist.md.
[08:34] Laura: thanks everyone, one more Q - can we do a quick demo of the schema validator during the bench run?
[08:38] Sara: yes we'll demo that in the infra handoff session, add to next call agenda.
[08:44] Evan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with next steps.

End of transcript.
